sql: SELECT avail_doy, value FROM climate WHERE index_id='oni' AND avail_season=2 ORDER BY avail_doy

# Season 2 planning check-in (day 60, still preseason — nightly decisions start ~doy 91/Apr 1)
- Confirmed via results.json: still 0 booked, full $2000/10 PTO, 0 rejected actions, season/cumulative
  rank 13 (tied at 0 with everyone — normal, nobody's nightly decisions have run yet since it's winter).
- **ONI update: still deep La Niña, not recovering.** doy 9 = -1.57, doy 40 = -1.48 (season 2). Basically
  flat/still strongly negative — no warming trend yet with ~30 days to go before April nightly decisions
  start. This is colder than any point in Season 1 (which ranged -1.54 to +1.5, avg ~0.06). Only 2 climate
  readings exist so far this season (monthly cadence), so next update likely lands around doy ~70.
  **Action: at the first nightly briefings in April, explicitly check the latest ONI reading before
  committing to the "front-load three_quarter spend in Apr-Jun" plan.** If ONI is still <-1 by then,
  treat Season 1's Apr-Jun three_quarter hit rates (~0.5-0.6/angler) as optimistic — pace slower, book
  smaller/cheaper (e.g. skip a marginal week) until fishdope yt_local or pier wtmp_c actually shows fish
  showing up locally, rather than trusting the calendar/seasonality table alone. If ONI has moved back
  toward neutral (>-0.5) by an April briefing, the original Season-1-based plan stands as written below.
- Table schema reference (from describe_tables, in case future turns need it):
  trips (per-boat counts, cls in {hd_am,hd_pm,hd_unspecified,hd_twilight,three_quarter,full_day,
  overnight,day_1_5}, yt=kept+released, anglers), schedule (boat/landing/cls, visible 14 days ahead,
  no counts), climate (index_id oni/pdo/npgo/mei_v2, monthly value), pier (wtmp_c hourly, Scripps),
  fishdope (yt_local/yt_all/migrated/stamp_kind + narrative text, roughly daily). Share formula:
  sum(yt)/(sum(anglers)+competitors) across all rows of that class+fish_date.
- No new boat-level or trip data this turn (still winter, all-zero season). Nothing to re-verify yet
  against the Season 1 boat list (San Diego/Seaforth, Mission Belle/Point Loma, Malihini/H&M) until
  Season 2 three_quarter trips start posting counts in April.

# Notes after Season 1 review (carried forward, still the core plan)

## Big finding: half-days are nearly dead for yellowtail
My persona leans toward cheap $80 half-days, but Season 1 data says that's a trap for THIS species:
- hd_am: 94% of trips caught ZERO yellowtail, avg rate 0.013 fish/angler.
- hd_pm: 93% zero, avg rate 0.014 fish/angler.
- three_quarter ($150): only 51% zero, avg rate 0.245 fish/angler — ~18x the half-day rate for <2x the price.
- overnight ($400): 62% zero, avg rate 0.356/angler.
- day_1_5 ($550): 75% zero, avg rate 0.477/angler — highest raw rate but priciest.
Ranked by yellowtail-per-dollar: three_quarter > overnight ≈ day_1_5 >> hd_am/hd_pm (half-days ~15-20x worse per dollar).
**Plan: treat THREE_QUARTER as my "cheap ticket" workhorse, not half-days.** Half-days only make sense
as a $0-PTO-cost weekend filler when nothing better is scheduled and budget is otherwise idle.

## Seasonality (doy ~91 = Apr 1; nightly decisions run Apr-Nov)
Avg rate by month (fish/angler), roughly, from Season 1 (a prior, not a guarantee — see ONI caveat above):
- Apr: hd 0.01-0.02, three_quarter 0.56, overnight 1.27, day_1_5 1.93 (best month overall, small-ish n early)
- May: three_quarter 0.54, overnight 0.40, day_1_5 0.44
- Jun: three_quarter 0.46, overnight 0.60, day_1_5 0.18
- Jul: everything craters (three_quarter 0.06, overnight 0.02, day_1_5 0.01) — dead zone, don't spend here
- Aug: still weak (three_quarter 0.04, overnight 0.24 — overnight has a small edge)
- Sep: still weak across the board (~0.04-0.06)
- Oct: BIG rebound, especially longer range — day_1_5 2.35, three_quarter 0.31, overnight 0.69
- Nov: day_1_5 1.86 still strong, three_quarter/overnight fade (0.06-0.13)
- Dec: mostly dead, small n

**$-per-fish ranking by month** confirms: Apr-Jun → three_quarter is the best value class. Oct-Nov →
day_1_5 pulls ahead of three_quarter even accounting for price (fall run). Jul-Sep is a value desert —
minimize spend, skip unless a boat has a hot recent report.

## Plan for pacing $2000 / 10 PTO across Apr-Nov (adjusted for La Niña risk)
- Front-load spend in Apr-Jun on three_quarter trips, BUT gate on ONI/fishdope first (see check-in above)
  — if the cold signal hasn't broken by April, book fewer/smaller early bets and hold more budget back
  for a possible Oct-Nov rebound rather than assuming Season-1 rates repeat.
- Aim to not blow >40% of budget before July, and less than that if ONI is still negative in April.
- Jul-Sep: go quiet — only cheap probes if fishdope/reports show a local warm push (check yt_local/
  migrated at each briefing), otherwise sit out.
- Save PTO for Oct-Nov day_1_5/overnight weekday trips (fall run pays off there); PTO must be committed
  14 days ahead — start watching forecasts/fishdope for the Oct push by mid-September so PTO commits
  land in time.
- Don't chase overnight/day_1.5 in the dead months (Jul-Sep) — rate/$ is worse there.

## Boats (three_quarter, Apr-Jun Season-1 window, n>=5)
Best combo of sample size + rate: San Diego (Seaforth, n=81, rate 0.61, 86% nonzero), Mission Belle
(Point Loma, n=61, rate 0.55, 77% nonzero), Malihini (H&M, n=73, rate 0.44, 74% nonzero). Pacific
Voyager/Voyager (Seaforth) had very high rates but tiny n (7-8) — could be noise, watch for repeat
performance before trusting. Re-verify against Season 2 actuals once three_quarter trips start posting
counts in April — did the same boats stay hot?

## To check every nightly briefing (Apr-Nov)
1. fishdope yt_local/yt_all/migrated/stamp_kind — is there a reported local push right now? Can override
   seasonal averages (e.g. an early or late warm pulse).
2. Recent-week fleet counts for the SPECIFIC boat being considered, not just the class average.
3. Water temp (pier wtmp_c) trend — a temp spike is a decent leading signal even in "dead" months.
4. ONI/climate index — log it alongside outcomes each time to build a real correlation across seasons.
   Currently still deep La Niña (-1.5-ish) as of doy 40, unchanged from doy 9 — watch for any recovery.
5. PTO 14-day-ahead lock-in — don't miss committing for an Oct/Nov weekday day_1_5/overnight; check
   forecast/fishdope trend ~2-3 weeks out.

## Strategy.py
Still the placeholder (books nothing) — nightly manual decisions drive Season 2 using the plan above.
Candidate for later: auto-commit PTO for Oct/Nov weekdays when a scheduled three_quarter/day_1_5 boat
has a strong recent count and budget/PTO remain; hard-avoid hd_am/hd_pm by default.

## Open questions for next planning turn
- Did Season 2's cold ONI actually suppress Apr-Jun three_quarter rates vs. Season 1, once real trips
  start posting? This is the big test of the La Niña caveat above.
- Did the same three_quarter boats (San Diego, Mission Belle, Malihini) stay hot in Season 2?
- Confirm three_quarter/other class prices stayed flat all season (rules say fixed — sanity check only).
- Did committing PTO early vs. late within the 14-day window ever matter, or is it a pure lock-in with
  no timing edge?
